paper.title_en: Quantifying the TKM-IKT ambiguity: translating the theoretical benchmark into experimental discriminants for future colliders
paper.abstract_en: This paper, the second of two companion works, translates the theoretical benchmark established in into quantitative predictions for high-energy $γγ$ interactions. We simultaneously confront the TKM and IKT dipole cross-section prescriptions across five representative saturation models (GBW, IIMS, rcBK, AGBS, WYKWC). Evaluating real and virtual cross sections, $F_2^γ$, and heavy-quark production, we demonstrate that the TKM--IKT discrepancy is an irreducible structural ambiguity reaching $48\pm12\%$ at LEP energies and expanding into the TeV regime. We propose three experimental discriminants for future colliders (ILC, CLIC, FCC-ee) --- emphasizing exclusive $γγ\to J/ψ+ J/ψ$ production where quadratic amplitude scaling ($[\mathcal{N}]^2$) magnifies the divergence --- elevating these comparisons from parameter choices to rigorous falsification tests of the foundational premises. Finally, an analytical universality test using GBW DIS parameters establishes the quantitative baseline required to falsify the underlying dipole--target analogy.
